case_title: Laut Kumar Yadav @ Kuri v. State of Uttar Pradesh
aggravating_circumstances: Attempted rape, resistance leading to murder, past conduct of eve teasing
mitigating_circumstances: Young age, no criminal antecedents, possibility of reform
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and Section 376 read with Section 511 IPC, sentenced to death
neutral_facts: The accused attempted to commit rape on an 18-year-old girl, leading to her murder. The prosecution relied on circumstantial evidence including a sniffer dog tracking the accused, recovery of a sickle used to cut the victim's neck, recovery of the accused's clothes, and the accused's past conduct of eve teasing the victim. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC and Section 376 read with Section 511 IPC, sentencing him to death. The High Court affirmed the conviction and death sentence. The Supreme Court partially allowed the appeal, commuting the death sentence to life imprisonment due to the accused's young age, lack of criminal antecedents, and the possibility of reform, while affirming the rest of the conviction and sentence.
